families.name: Explicit HTTP forward requests
families.rationale: Only the audited direct HTTP/1 forwarding forms are lowered; broader Squid request, protocol, and cache semantics are not represented.

families.name: CONNECT tunnels
families.rationale: The bounded explicit CONNECT form has wire, failure, half-close, byte, idle, lifetime, and shutdown coverage.

families.name: Includes and source ordering
families.rationale: Deterministic file and glob includes are checked with source identity and provenance; conditional and unrestricted native configuration behavior is outside the importer.

families.name: ACL definitions and access ordering
families.rationale: Source, exact port, proxy-authentication, built-in, and ordered HTTP access forms are audited; destination lookup, time, regex, and asynchronous ACLs remain open.

families.name: Proxy authentication
families.rationale: The bounded Basic htpasswd form is integrated; Digest, Negotiate, NTLM, helper protocols, and broader authentication controls are not equivalent.

families.name: Resolver selection
families.rationale: Explicit finite nameserver lists lower into the forward resolver; Squid DNS tuning and lookup policy do not.

families.name: Header privacy and access
families.rationale: Delete forwarded-address metadata and disable Via are enforced; header ACL, replacement, and arbitrary mutation forms are blocked.

families.name: Logging and audit output
families.rationale: Disabled native access logging is represented; Squid log formats, rotation, cache logs, and management logging are not reproduced.

families.name: Memory and persistent HTTP caching
families.rationale: The Squid importer targets direct non-caching forwarding and must not advertise cache admission, storage, eviction, or reuse parity.

families.name: Freshness, revalidation, ranges, and collapsed forwarding
families.rationale: refresh_pattern and related cache freshness behavior are not runtime-owned; parsed refresh rules are only retained as explicit externalization evidence.

families.name: Parent and sibling cache peers
families.rationale: Ordered static HTTP parent peers and global direct fallback rules lower into the bounded HTTP/1 peer policy; sibling, dynamic, credentialed, hierarchy, and ICP forms remain blocked.

families.name: External ACL and URL rewrite helpers
families.rationale: Helper process protocols, lifecycle, concurrency, timeouts, and failure semantics are not implemented and cannot be inferred from parsed arguments.

families.name: ICAP and eCAP adaptation
families.rationale: Adaptation service negotiation and content transformation are outside the direct-forward runtime.

families.name: Transparent interception and TPROXY
families.rationale: Intercept, tproxy, WCCP, source preservation, and kernel policy-routing behavior are not owned by the socket proxy runtime.

families.name: TLS bump and certificate mimicry
families.rationale: TLS interception changes origin identity and requires a separate high-risk certificate and policy architecture; it is not an HTTPS-origin forwarding claim.

families.name: Delay pools and traffic shaping
families.rationale: Hierarchical Squid bandwidth accounting and delay-pool scheduling are not represented by the forward service limits.

families.name: FTP proxy and listing behavior
families.rationale: FTP proxying and generated listings are not part of the maintained direct HTTP/1 compatibility line.

families.name: ICP, HTCP, WCCP, SNMP, and Cache Manager
families.rationale: Legacy datagram, router-cooperation, and native management protocols are not planned as Squid parity targets for this daemon.

families.name: Process, worker, and deployment controls
families.rationale: Process ownership and deployment settings are externalized or owned by OxiRoute supervision rather than translated into Squid runtime behavior.

families.name: ESI and content processing
families.rationale: ESI and cache-coupled content processing have no direct-forward runtime equivalent in this scope.

families.name: Obsolete target-version directives
families.rationale: The target checkout documents these legacy names as removed or obsolete; they must not be classified as supported compatibility.

entries.form: deterministic file or byte-sorted glob include
entries.rationale: Static include expansion is bounded and provenance-preserving, but is not a complete Squid preprocessor implementation.

entries.form: explicit HTTP listener endpoint without options
entries.rationale: The exact no-option endpoint lowers to the forward HTTP/1 listener and is covered by imported runtime and rejection tests.

entries.form: intercept, tproxy, accel, ssl-bump, name, defaultsite, or other port option
entries.rationale: Port options alter interception, acceleration, or TLS behavior that the direct listener cannot reproduce.
The forward importer does not turn a native HTTPS or bump listener into an equivalent canonical listener.
The exact disabled form is consumed without silently dropping enabled Squid logging behavior.

entries.form: enabled native access logging or custom format
entries.rationale: Native access-log destinations and format macros are not equivalent to the structured forward audit path.
A finite unique non-special nameserver list is retained by the canonical resolver policy and has failure coverage.
The audited source CIDR form lowers into ordered forward access conditions and is exercised through the imported runtime.
An exact port ACL is used for the bounded CONNECT guard and is rejected when ranges or ambiguous guards would change policy.
The exact required-authentication predicate is lowered with the audited Basic credential path and missing-credential failure coverage.

entries.form: destination, time, regex, external, asynchronous, or other ACL type
entries.rationale: The strict importer blocks ACL types without a semantics-preserving canonical matcher.

entries.form: ordered allow or deny rule over audited named and built-in ACLs
entries.rationale: First-match ordering, native default action, and the audited ACL predicates are retained in the forward access policy.

entries.form: one exact unconditional deny CONNECT !port guard before an allow
entries.rationale: The exact CONNECT guard is required for safe port inference and is covered by positive tunnel and rejection tests.

entries.form: conditional, ranged, reordered, multiple, or missing CONNECT guard
entries.rationale: The importer fails closed instead of guessing CONNECT destination-port policy.

entries.form: Basic program, realm, credential TTL, and case policy used by the audited importer
entries.rationale: The exact Basic htpasswd form is lowered and exercised through authenticated runtime success and failure paths.

entries.form: helper concurrency, UTF-8, key extras, or other unsupported setting
entries.rationale: Helper setting semantics are not accepted as if they were enforced by the Basic runtime.

entries.form: Digest, Negotiate, NTLM, or other non-Basic scheme
entries.rationale: Non-Basic challenge and helper protocols are not implemented by the canonical forward authentication model.
The exact privacy form maps to the canonical forward header policy and is exercised in the imported runtime path.
The exact disabled form maps to the canonical Via policy and is not silently widened to other modes.
Header ACL evaluation is not represented by the bounded canonical header policy.
Arbitrary Squid replacement templates do not have an equivalent bounded forward mutation.
The path is retained only as deployment evidence; OxiRoute supervision owns process state.
Worker process coordination is owned by supervision and is not translated into a Squid-compatible runtime setting.
Direct forwarding does not implement Squid cache admission or bypass semantics.
The importer may type the value for diagnostics but the direct runtime has no Squid cache store to configure.
Persistent Squid storage, recovery, quota, eviction, and ownership are not implemented by this importer scope.
Freshness rules are parsed and externalized for explicit operator review; they are not enforced by direct forwarding.
Collapsed forwarding is cache coordination behavior and must not be confused with the direct request path.

entries.form: static parent with a host, HTTP port, ICP port 0, and no options
entries.rationale: The exact static parent form lowers in source order into the bounded HTTP/1 peer policy with finite attempts and runtime wire coverage.

entries.form: sibling, multicast, nonzero ICP, credentials, hierarchy, or any peer option
entries.rationale: Peer hierarchy, authentication, ICP, and option semantics cannot be represented by the ordered static parent runtime.
Peer access ordering cannot be lowered without the peer hierarchy runtime.
The exact global rule requires direct fallback and is lowered into the bounded peer policy.
The exact global rule denies direct fallback after ordered static parent attempts and is lowered into the bounded peer policy.

entries.form: conditional, named-ACL, or multiple direct-routing rules
entries.rationale: Conditional directness requires hierarchy-aware request evaluation that is not represented by the bounded static peer policy.
ICP is a legacy datagram peer protocol and is outside the maintained compatibility line.
HTCP is a legacy cache peer protocol with no direct-forward equivalent.
External ACL helper requests and result caching are not represented by the synchronous bounded matcher set.
Helper-driven URL rewriting cannot be approximated by a static destination policy.

entries.form: cache key or Store ID helper
entries.rationale: Store ID helpers are cache-coupled and have no direct-forward runtime target.
Adaptation negotiation and body transformation are not implemented in the direct-forward service.
Adaptation chain ordering, iteration, and failure behavior have no canonical representation here.

entries.form: TLS bump step and certificate mimicry policy
entries.rationale: TLS bump is a separate interception and certificate-issuance feature, not HTTPS-origin verification.

entries.form: TLS bump certificate database or validator helper
entries.rationale: Certificate mimicry helpers cannot be reduced to the ordinary outbound TLS identity model.

entries.form: native TLS outgoing option set not in the audited form
entries.rationale: Native TLS option combinations are not accepted without an equivalence proof for the canonical origin policy.
Delay pool accounting is not equivalent to finite connection, body, or timeout limits.
The direct-forward runtime supports HTTP/1 and CONNECT, not Squid FTP proxy/listing behavior.
WCCP requires kernel/router cooperation and is not a socket-level forward-proxy capability.

entries.form: SNMP or Cache Manager management endpoint
entries.rationale: OxiRoute management and metrics are not a wire-compatible Squid Cache Manager or SNMP endpoint.
The target checkout documents this legacy option as removed; it is not a current compatibility surface.
The target checkout documents the old announcement directives as removed in Squid 6.x.

entries.form: removed or replaced legacy HTTP and DNS options
entries.rationale: The target checkout marks these compatibility names obsolete or replaced by current directives.
